questions.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\frac{1}{x}\,i+\frac{1}{y}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=2{t}^{2}+2$ and $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{2{t}^{2}+2}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{arctan}⁡t}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡t)\,j \\  & =4t\,i+\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{2}+2}\,i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{arctan}⁡t}\,j)\cdot (4t\,i+\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2{t}^{2}+2}\cdot 4t+\frac{1}{\operatorname{arctan}⁡t}\cdot \frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+1}+\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{2t\operatorname{arctan}⁡t+1}{({t}^{2}+1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =\frac{2(1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡1+1}{({1}^{2}+1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡1} \\  & =\frac{(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}+1)}{(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{\pi +2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

∇f(x,y)=2x\,i+2y\,j.

First, we substitute $x={e}^{-t}$ and $y={e}^{t}$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2{e}^{-t}\,i+2{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j \\  & =(-{e}^{-t})\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2{e}^{-t}\,i+2{e}^{t}\,j)\cdot ((-{e}^{-t})\,i+{e}^{t}\,j) \\  & =2{e}^{-t}\cdot (-{e}^{-t})+2{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t} \\  & =2{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨t-1,3,2t⟩$ at the point $t=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})),\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})),\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}},\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}},\frac{2z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t-1,$ $y=3$ and $z=2t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\frac{2(t-1)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}},\frac{2(3)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}},\frac{2(2t)}{(t-1)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2t)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),2t⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10},\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}⟩\cdot ⟨1,0,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{2t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 1+\frac{6}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 0+\frac{4t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2t-2+8t}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10} \\  & =\frac{10t-2}{5{t}^{2}-2t+10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(0))] & =\frac{10(0)-2}{5(0)^{2}-2(0)+10} \\  & =\frac{-2}{10} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,k \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,j+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1,$ $y=2t$ and $z={t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k)\cdot (\,i+2\,j+2t\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 1+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2t(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)(1+t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)+{e}^{y})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\,i+{e}^{y}\,j+\frac{1}{z}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,y={t}^{2},$ and $z=\frac{1}{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+{e}^{{t}^{2}}\,j+t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2t\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+{e}^{{t}^{2}}\,j+t\,k)\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2t\,j-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,k) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}+2t{e}^{{t}^{2}}-\frac{t}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡t+2t{e}^{{t}^{2}}-\frac{1}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$
